info.title: Waypoint API
info.summary: Open items, dependencies and wake-ups for a group of agent sessions.
info.description:
The HTTP API of `waypointd`. Everything else (the MCP server, `wp`, the deliverers) is a client
of it. The prose that goes with this file is `docs/API.md`; where the two differ, this file is
the contract and the prose is a bug.

Conventions:
- JSON in and out, UTF-8. Times are RFC 3339. Waypoint answers in UTC with a `Z` suffix; input
  must carry a zone (`Z` or an offset) and is converted to UTC. A day (`when` with precision
  `day`) is a plain date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the deployment's time zone.
- Every request but `GET /v1/health` carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Unknown fields in a request body are refused (`invalid`), never stored.
- Absent fields in a response are never used for "unknown": a field without a value is `null`
  or an empty list.

port.description: Waypoint's built-in default port; deployments usually set their own.

tags.name: views
tags.description: Read models for pages. Every flag and edge a page needs is in them.

tags.name: deliveries
tags.description: Deliverers fetch the messages that fell due for their recipients and confirm them.

tags.name: clients
tags.description: Register clients and manage their tokens. Coordinators and humans only.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Comma-separated states, or `all`. Default `next,running,waiting` (the open ones).

parameters.name: waiting_on
parameters.description: Only items with an open condition on an item owned by this client.

parameters.name: waits_on_human
parameters.description: Only items with an open condition on an item owned by a human.

parameters.name: changed_since
parameters.description: Only items updated after this time (any state, so pages see items that closed).

201.description: The new item, with its derived state and flags.

get.summary: One item, with its history and what waits on it.

patch.description:
Only the fields present change; `null` clears a field that may be empty. Who may change
what is in `docs/API.md` (Permissions).

post.summary: Put a decision to a human for this item, in one step.
post.description:
Creates a `decision` item owned by the human, with the question, and makes this item wait
on it, in one transaction: either both happen or neither. The caller needs the right to
change this item. Asked again with the same human, title and question while that decision
is open and this item waits on it, Waypoint answers the existing decision (200) instead of
creating a second one, so a retry is safe.

201.description: The decision was created and this item now waits on it.

200.description: The same question was open already; nothing changed.
The recurrences, by `next_at` (paused and stopped ones last), then id.

post.description:
Same rules as creating an item: the content check, the length limits, and permissions (an
agent may create one for itself or hand it to another agent; one owned by a human is created
and changed only by that human or a coordinator). Its first occurrence falls due
at `next_at`.

patch.summary: Change, pause, resume or stop a recurrence.
patch.description:
A changed schedule takes effect from the next occurrence; open occurrences stay as they are.
Resuming starts from the next scheduled time without catching up the paused span. `stopped`
is final.

post.summary: A job on a timer reports a run.
post.description:
For a recurrence with `checkin: true`. `ok` closes the oldest open occurrence as done, with
the note; `failed` drops it with the note, so its owner is told. A check-in when no
occurrence is open is recorded in the recurrence's history and answered with
`occurrence: null`. Allowed for the client named in `checkin_by` (which may do nothing
else with the recurrence), the owner, coordinators and humans.

put.description:
Any agent, human or coordinator may create a new track; an existing one is replaced only
by its lead, a coordinator or a human.

get.summary: Read model for the time page.
get.description:
Items, dependency edges and derived flags around a window of time. The page does the
bucketing itself. Which items are included is in `docs/API.md` (Views).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the window. Default now minus `done_days`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the window. Default now plus 9 days.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: Comma-separated track ids; default all tracks that are not archived.

get.summary: Read model for the "you first" page.
get.description:
That human's open items, the ones that are their turn first and longest-waiting first, each
with the chain it unblocks and, if it is not their turn yet, what it is waiting for.

get.summary: Fetch my delivery queue (deliverers only), with a long-poll.
get.description:
Returns the messages that fell due for the recipients registered with the calling
deliverer, are not confirmed, and are not under an unexpired lease (never handed out, or
handed out more than `lease_seconds` ago). Withdrawn messages (see `docs/API.md`) are never
returned. If there are none, Waypoint holds the request open for
up to `wait` seconds and answers as soon as one falls due, or with an empty list at the end.
A message handed out and not confirmed within `lease_seconds` is handed out again, with
`attempt` increased.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to hold the request open when the queue is empty.

200.description: The messages, oldest `fell_due_at` first; possibly none.

get.summary: My own messages, in full, newest first.
get.description:
Every message Waypoint sent the caller (the recipient), with its full text and what became of
it. A recipient whose deliverer only types a short line ("ref" mode) reads the details here,
e.g. of an outage summary. Not for deliverers, which read their queue at /v1/deliveries.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only messages that fell due at or after this time.

post.description:
Idempotent: confirming the same message again returns the first confirmation unchanged.
A message of another deliverer is answered `not_found`.

post.summary: Register a client. Its token is in the answer, once.

201.description: The client and its token. Waypoint keeps only the token's hash.

patch.summary: Change a client's label or deliverer, or retire it.
patch.description:
Retiring is refused (`invalid`, field `retired`) while the client owns open items (hand
them to another owner or close them first), and for the coordinator (the configured one,
or the last coordinator when none is configured). A retired client's token stops working
and its deliverer registration ends: its waiting messages go to the coordinator if a
deliverer reaches it, and are withdrawn otherwise.

200.description: The client as it is now.

post.summary: Replace a client's token. The old one stops working at once.

get.summary: A server-sent stream of changes, so pages update live.
get.description:
`text/event-stream`. After every committed change Waypoint sends one event per changed
item (`event: item`, data `{id, version, state, updated_at}`) and per changed track
(`event: track`, data `{id}`), and per changed recurrence (`event: recurrence`, data `{id, version,
state, next_at}`), each with an `id:` of the form `<run>-<seq>` (`run` changes
when Waypoint restarts; `seq` increases). A page reloads what it shows
when it sees one. Lines starting with `:` are heartbeats. Reconnecting with the
`Last-Event-ID` header sends what was missed, or `event: reset` (data `{reason}`) when that
is too far back, the id is from before a restart, or the reader was too slow: then reload
everything. The token goes in the
Authorization header like everywhere else, never in the URL; a browser page reads the
stream through its own backend.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The `id` of the last event received, `<run>-<seq>`.

get.summary: What needs attention, for monitoring and the coordinator's checks.

200.description: The status. `ok` is false when any list is not empty or the scheduler is behind.

get.summary: Counts for a metrics collector, in the Prometheus text format. Needs a token like everything else.

bearer.description: One token per client, issued by `wp client add`. Never put it in a URL.

Invalid.description: `invalid`: the request is malformed (bad field, value, query parameter or unknown field).

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`: no token or not a valid one. Nothing else is revealed.

Forbidden.description: `forbidden`: the caller's role may not do this.

NotFound.description: `not_found`: no such item, track, human or delivery (or not the caller's delivery).

Conflict.description: `loop`: the write would close a loop of conditions (`cycle` names it); `version_conflict`: `if_version` did not match.

Content.description: `content`: a field looks like it holds a secret, an address or other data that must not be stored. `field` names it; the offending text is never echoed.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 with seconds and a zone. Responses are always UTC with `Z`.

Day.description: A calendar day in the deployment's time zone.

ClientName.description: A client's stable name, agent or human (`agent-a`, `alice`).

Kind.description: `decision`: a human chooses; `approval`: a human says go; `event`: happens at a time by itself.

State.description: `next` and `waiting` are derived by Waypoint; `running`, `done`, `dropped` are set by the owner.

Role.description: `unknown`: the name is used by an item but no such client exists (any more).

Delay.description: Minutes, hours or days after the due time, e.g. `0m`, `90m`, `1h`, `2d`.

Title.description: One line, readable without context. No line breaks or other control characters in a request; text stored before 0.2 may still hold them in answers.

Label.description: Short form of the title for tight places (timeline stops). No line breaks or other control characters in a request; text stored before 0.2 may still hold them in answers.

Note.description: One line. No line breaks or other control characters in a request; text stored before 0.2 may still hold them in answers.

Condition.description: A condition as Waypoint reports it.

recommendation.description: The asking owner's recommendation, usually one of the options.

AnswerAtInput.description:
Where the person answers a decision or approval: as a comment on an issue or pull request
(its URL), or in a session (its client name; never a session URL or id).

AnswerAt.description: `AnswerAtInput` as Waypoint reports it; `default` is true when nobody set it.

When.description:
When it happens. With precision `minute` or `hour`, `start` and `end` are timestamps
(truncated to the precision); with precision `day` they are days. `end` is for spans
(a soak from–until).

to.description: The human to push to; required for `notify`, not allowed otherwise.

caught_up.description: Taken after Waypoint was down, as the furthest step reached by then.

RiskSource.description: An item upstream (directly or further back) that is late or dropped.

due_at.description: That item's due time, when `why` is `late`.

Item.description: An item as Waypoint reports it.

label.description: Short form for tight places; `null` means the page shortens the title.

waited_on_by.description: Items that have this item as a condition (met or not).

answer_at.description:
For decisions and approvals: where the person answers. When none was set and the item
was created by an agent, it is that agent's session, with `default: true`. `null` for
other kinds, or when there is neither.

running_until.description:
While `running`: until when the owner's claim lasts. Renewed by the owner's updates;
when it passes the owner gets a `running_check`. `null` in every other state.

running_overdue.description:
Running, past `running_until`, and the owner was asked whether it still runs: a page
can draw "running?". It goes back to `next` if the owner doesn't update it in time.

overdue.description: This item's own ladder; empty means the deployment's default ladder applies.

note.description: One line of current status; for a dropped item, the reason.

late.description: Past `due_at` and not done or dropped.

recurrence.description: The recurrence this item is an occurrence of; `null` for an ordinary item.

occurrence_at.description: For an occurrence, the scheduled time it stands for; `null` otherwise.

at_risk_from.description: Why it is at risk; empty when `at_risk` is false.

overdue_steps.description: Ladder steps taken since the current due time was set, oldest first.

updated_by.description: The client of the last change; `null` when the last change was Waypoint's own.

done_at.description: When it became done or dropped.

by.description: The client; `null` for Waypoint's own (derived states, the scheduler).

owner.description: Default the caller. An agent may create items for another owner (handing over).

state.description: Only `running` may be given; otherwise Waypoint derives `next` or `waiting`.

running_until.description: With `state` running only; default now plus the deployment's running lease.

question.description: Required for `decision`, optional for `approval`, refused otherwise.

answer_at.description:
Decisions and approvals only. Required when `links` hold an issue or pull request
(say where the answer goes); otherwise it defaults to the creating agent's session.

if_version.description: Refuse with `version_conflict` unless the item is at this version.

state.description:
`running`, `done`, `dropped` as given (`dropped` needs a `note`, the reason). `next` and
`waiting` both mean "not running (any more)": Waypoint then derives which one applies;
on a done or dropped item they reopen it (dependents of a reopened done item that were
`next` go back to `waiting`).

running_until.description:
For a running item (or one this request sets running): until when it runs; in the
future. Without it, the owner's updates renew the lease to now plus the default.

add_waits_on.description: Adds conditions to the list (already present ones are ignored).

answer_at.description: Set or change where the answer goes; `null` goes back to the default.
Where the person answers; required when `links` hold an issue or pull request.

label.description: Display name; the client name if none is set.

Owners.description: Every client name used in the view (owners, leads, `created_by`), with its role.

Edge.description: `to` waits on `from`. Both are in the view's `items`.

tz.description: The deployment's IANA time zone, for display and for days.

done_days.description: How long done and dropped items stay visible.

items.description: Ordered by track order, then dependency order, then `id`.

upcoming.description:
The coming occurrences of active recurrences within the window, oldest first: computed,
never stored (an occurrence becomes an item only when it falls due). A page may draw them
as faint markers.

ready.description: It is the human's turn (`next` or `running`); false while it still waits.

since.description: When it became the human's turn (`ready`), or when it was created otherwise.

unblocks.description: Open items that wait on this one, directly or further on, nearest first.

on_the_way.description: The open items this one still waits for, directly or further back, nearest first. Empty when `ready`.

entries.description: The human's open items; ready ones first, each group by `since`, oldest first.

tracks.description: The tracks of the items in this view.

items.description: Every item the entries name (the human's own, their chains), each once.

recurrences.description: The human's own recurrences (active and paused), by `next_at`.

Interval.description: Minutes, hours or days, e.g. `15m`, `2h`, `1d`; at least 5 minutes.

ClockTime.description: A wall-clock time, `HH:MM`, in the recurrence's zone.

Schedule.description:
When a recurrence occurs. Times are wall-clock times in `tz` (default: the deployment's
zone). A time that doesn't exist that day (clocks go forward) fires at the first valid minute
after it; a time that occurs twice (clocks go back) fires once, the first time. An interval
runs on absolute time, anchored at `from` (default: when the recurrence was created).

monthly.description: The day of the month, 1 to 28, or `last`.

overdue.description: The occurrences' own ladder; empty means the deployment's default.

window.description: How long an occurrence may take; its `due_at` is the occurrence time plus this.

overlap.description:
When the next occurrence falls due while the previous one is open: `skip` it (a history
line on the open one), `replace` the open one (dropped with a reason), or `allow` both.

catch_up.description: After Waypoint's own downtime, one late occurrence for the missed span (`latest`), or none.

checkin.description: A job on a timer reports each run (`POST /v1/recurrences/{id}/checkin`).

checkin_by.description:
The client a job checks in as. It may check in and do nothing else with the recurrence;
set by whoever may change the recurrence.

next_at.description: When the next occurrence falls due; `null` when paused or stopped.

last_at.description: The scheduled time of the last occurrence (created, skipped or caught up), if any.

open_occurrence.description: The oldest occurrence that is still open, if any (the one a check-in closes).

occurrence.description: The occurrence the check-in closed (done for `ok`, dropped for `failed`), or `null` when none was open.

state.description: `pending`: not confirmed yet; the others as its deliverer confirmed it, or withdrawn by Waypoint.

settled_at.description: When it was confirmed or withdrawn; `null` while pending.

kind.description: What the message is about; see `docs/API.md` (Deliveries). An open set: new kinds may be added, and readers ignore kinds they don't know.

item.description: The item the message is about, if any.

items.description: Other items it names (for `unblocked`, the item that was done).

attempt.description: 2 or more when handed out again.

late.description: Set when the message goes out later than it fell due for a known reason.

text.description: The full message for an agent, ready to type in.

summary.description: Title and owner only; the only text a push adapter may send.

lease_seconds.description: An unconfirmed message is handed out again after this long.

result.description: `undeliverable`: the adapter gave up (for tmux, after 30 minutes); Waypoint escalates it.

detail.description: Why it gave up. Quoted to the coordinator, so it passes the content check (`422 content`).

deliverer.description: The deliverer that reaches this client, if any.

last_seen.description: For a deliverer, its last fetch; otherwise null.

retired.description: Retire the client. There is no un-retiring.

token.description: The client's token. Shown only in this answer; store it in a file only its user can read.

since.description: Late since (due time), last updated (running), or created (unknown owner).

behind.description: No pass for more than a minute.

deliverers.description: Every deliverer that serves at least one recipient.

recipients_without_deliverer.description: Clients that own open items or have waiting messages but no deliverer.

stuck_deliveries.description: Messages not confirmed 30 minutes after they fell due.

unknown_owners.description: Open items whose owner is not a registered, unretired client.

running_stale.description: Items `running` for more than a day without an update.

coordinator.description:
Who hears about escalations, undeliverable messages and outages: the configured
coordinator, or the first live one. `ok` is false without a live one.

missed_checkins.description: Open, late occurrences of recurrences with `checkin` (a job didn't report its run).

message.description: For humans; never echoes the request or a token.

cycle.description: For `loop`, the items of the loop, first one repeated at the end.
